items.text: An unstable crane began spinning out of control a top a skyscraper in remnants of Hurricane Zeta winds in Manhattan, New York City. The crane repeatedly hit the building, and it sent debris plummeting to the ground from an 84-story tower that was under construction. Authorities closed off four blocks in midtown to prevent injuries; however, no injuries were reported. When fire crews arrived at the scene, they could not see the top of the building due to heavy wind and fog. The crane is designed to withstand winds of up to 160 kmph and to spin in the wind; however, officials are trying to determine what caused the debris to fall. Difficult words: remnant (the remains), plummet (to fall down at a high speed), midtown (the center of a city), withstand (to resist). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hurricane Zeta hit the east coast of the US, and it caused many problems in several US states. Strong winds that remained after the hurricane caused a crane to spin in New York City. On Tuesday, the crane started to spin out of control which scared many local people. Debris fell off an 84-story tower that the crane was working on. Authorities closed several streets around the tower because there was high risk that somebody would get hurt. When fire officers arrived, they could not see the top of the tower because of wind and fog. Cranes can resist winds of up to 160 kmph and they spin in the wind. Officials want to find out why the debris fell down. Difficult words: crane (a large and tall machine that people use to move heavy things and to build houses), spin (to turn around quickly), debris (pieces of rubbish or trash or remains of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hurricane Zeta brings strong winds to the east coast of the US. People in Manhattan, New York, see something unusual on Tuesday. A crane is working on top of a tall building. The building is 84 stories tall. The crane starts to turn around quickly in the wind. The crane gets out of control. Debris falls down. Authorities must close several streets around the crane. The streets are dangerous for people. Fire officers arrive. They cannot see the top of the building. The reason is wind and fog. Cranes are very strong. They can stand up in winds of 160 kmph. They spin in the wind. But the debris is a problem. Officials want to know why it falls down. Difficult words: crane (a large and tall machine that people use to build houses and to move heavy things), story (a level of a building), debris (smaller pieces of something that breaks). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Belgian chocalatier , Pierre Marcolini, has been crowned the world’s best pastry chef by a jury of independent reporters, enhancing Belgium’s reputation as a producer of top-class chocolate. Marcolini said that The Marcolini company had received recognition after 25 years of existence and that the title of world champion had been bestowed upon the whole company and all people who followed him. Marcolini’s aim was to transform and modernize the world of pastry and the world of chocolate. Marcolini travels the world to find the finest cocoa beans directly from growers, and he personally controls every stage of the production process. He is one of the few chocalatiers to roast cocoa beans himself. Today, he sells his chocolates as luxury gifts with boxes selling for over €100 or over $129. Difficult words: chocalatier (a person or company who makes or sells chocolate candy), reputation (the beliefs or opinions that are generally held about someone or something), bestow (to present an honor or gift to someone). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Pierre Marcolini is a Belgian chocalatier who was born in 1964. He worked for famous companies in Belgium and France before he opened his own first shop in 1995. His dream was to change the world of chocolate and to make it more modern. In his life, Marcolini received several prizes, and recently, World Pastry Stars organized a competition to win the title of the world’s best pastry chef. Marcolini won the title and he proved that Belgium makes the best chocolate. Marcolini travels the world to find the finest cocoa beans. He speaks to growers and he controls all the steps of making his chocolate. He is one of the few chocolatiers who roast cocoa beans himself. He sells special chocolate gift boxes that cost more than €100 or more than $129. Difficult words: chocalatier (a person or company that makes and sells chocolate candy), prove (to confirm), fine (of very high quality, making (the steps to make something)). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pierre Marcolini comes from Belgium. He is a chocalatier. It means that he makes and sells chocolate candy. Marcolini opens his own chocolate shop in 1995. 25 years later, Marcolini wins a special title . He is the best pastry chef in the world. It confirms that Belgium makes the best chocolate. Marcolini changes the world of chocolate. He makes it modern and attractive . Marcolini wants to use only the best cocoa beans. Cocoa beans are a fruit that we use to make chocolate. He speaks to people who grow cocoa. He prepares the cocoa beans himself. Only a few chocolatiers in the world do it. Marcolini sells chocolate gift boxes. They cost more than €100 or $129. Difficult words: title (a name for someone as a honor), pastry (cakes and tarts), confirm (to say that something is true), the world of (the business or the people that do something), attractive (pretty or pleasing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The founder of the American multi-level marketing company Nxivm, Keith Raniere, was once a self-improvement guru who had clients from New York to Hollywood. Between 1998 and 2020, the company held personal development seminars; however, the organization also faced multiple accusations of systemic sexual abuse. Last year, Raniere was found guilty on charges of sex trafficking, racketeering , and possession of child pornography. On Tuesday, Raniere was sentenced to 120 years in prison on criminal convictions for sexually abusing many of his female followers. He said in court that he had no remorse because he believed that he was innocent of the charges. On Tuesday, some of Raniere’s victims arrived at the courthouse for the sentencing, and they told of widespread abuses in the early 2000s. Difficult words: multi-level marketing (a business practice in which a seller earns money from both direct sales and from the sales of his recruits), guru (a spiritual teacher), systemic (a problem that is in all parts or systems of an organization), racketeer (to get money by threatening people), remorse (deep regret or guilt) You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Between 1998 and 2020, Keith Raniere was an American guru . Many Hollywood stars and famous people attended his meetings. Raniere also started a multi-level marketing company that was located in New York State. Many of Raniere’s followers said that he abused them and that he called them his sex slaves. Last year, the court found Raniere guilty of sex trafficking and for keeping child pornography. He also threatened people to get money from them. On Tuesday, a court sent Raniere to prison for 120 years. Raniere said that he did not feel sorry because he did nothing wrong. Difficult words: guru (a spiritual teacher), multi-level marketing (a kind of business when a seller gets money from his sales and sales of people who work under him), sex trafficking (moving people to places and getting money from their sexual activities). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Keith Raniere is an American guru. A guru is a spiritual teacher. He helps people live better lives. Raniere is a guru between 1998 – 2020. Many Hollywood stars and famous people visit him. Raniere starts a company. The company recruits people. The company gets money from their sales. Some people find this type of business strange. Raniere’s company makes some unusual business activities. Soon, people start to say that Raniere’s abuses them. Last week, a court sends Raniere to prison for 120 years. He is guilty of sexual business with people. He also threatens people to get money from them. He has sex slaves . Raniere says that he does nothing wrong. Difficult words: recruit (to select people and make them join a company), abuse (to use something or someone in a bad way), threaten (to say that you will hurt someone if he or she does not do what you want), slave (a person who belongs to someone and he must do everything that the other person wants). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

If you have been dreaming of owning a Ferrari, the 2021 Ferrari Roma is going to be your best bet. The car is 611- horsepower , and its top speed is 320 kmph. Its eight-speed paddle shifting transmission and rear-wheel drive can make the car accelerate from 0 to 100 kmph in 3.4 seconds. Ferrari Roma combines the classic beautiful lines of the Ferrari heritage with the modern, most accessible vehicle that Ferrari has come up with to date. The 2021 Ferrari Roma starts at $216,670, and it is set to go on sale in spring 2021. It may be the last Ferrari ever without having some sort of hybrid electric components. Difficult words: horsepower (the unit used to measure the power of an engine), paddle shifting transmission (paddles that allow the driver to change gears on an automatic transmission), heritage (history, where someone or something comes from), hybrid (combining two different elements). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ferrari has introduced a new car, the 2021 Ferrari Roma. The car is going to be on sale in spring 2021, and its price starts at $216,670. The car is 611- horsepower , and it can reach the speed of 320 kmph. There is a lot of leg and head room, so it is comfortable even for tall people. The brakes react quickly and the steering is light. There is a back seat, but it is suitable for a handbag or some shopping bags. The car combines the classic Ferrari lines with modern style. It is possible that this is the last Ferrari car that does not have any hybrid electric parts. Difficult words: horsepower (the unit that is used to measure the power of a car), brake (a device that stops or slows a machine when a person presses it), steering (a device that controls where a car is going), hybrid (when the car combines petrol or gasoline and electricity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ferrari is an Italian company. This company makes sports and racing cars. Ferrari introduces a new car. It is the 2021 Ferrari Roma. The car is very special. It has beautiful lines. They are typical for Ferrari cars. But Ferrari Roma is very modern, too. The car’s top speed is 320 kmph. It has eight gears . It can go from 0 to 100 kmph in 3.4 seconds. It is very light and easy to drive the car. The price of the car starts at almost $216,700. The car will be on sale in spring 2021. It is possible that Ferrari Roma is the last Ferrari car without any hybrid electric parts. Difficult words: introduce (to present something for the first time), gear (a part of a car that makes is possible to go faster or slower), hybrid (when the car uses petrol or gasoline as well as electricity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Nigeria, the uproar over police brutality has reached a boiling point after the military allegedly shot at peaceful protesters on October 20 th . However, government officials claimed that there were no casualties. Videos shot by protesters caught the sound of shooting as protesters sat on the ground chanting and waving Nigerian flags. A video also shows a soldier kicking at a barricade . However, the Nigerian army denied that there had been any soldiers at the scene. In the past three years, Amnesty International recorded more than 80 incidents of police brutality, and they say that the Special Anti-Robbery Squad, SARS, routinely used torture and brutality to get information from victims. SARS was disbanded in early October; however, protesters say that it will not solve the problem because the same officers will be moved to other newly formed units. Difficult words: uproar (angry public criticism of something), boiling point (the moment when anger or excitement turns violent), barricade (a wall or other object to keep people or objects away from one another), disband (to break up an existing organization). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People in Nigeria protested against police brutality . The people’s anger increased after a recent incident when the military shot at protesters. The protest took place on October 20 th, and it was quite peaceful. Protesters shot videos of people sitting on the ground. They were singing and waving Nigerian flags. Then it was possible to hear some shooting in the background. Some videos showed soldiers, but the Nigerian army said that there were no soldiers at the place. In the past three years, there have been more than 80 stories of police brutality. There was a special police unit called SARS, and it often used brutality to get information from people. Officials broke up SARS in early October, and they made a new police unit. A lot of people do not believe that this will stop police brutality. Difficult words: police brutality (when police use strong force against people), increase (to get bigger), incident (a very good or bad event), military (soldiers). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in Nigeria protest against the police. This means they say that they are not happy. SARS is in Nigeria. SARS is a special police unit . It starts in 1992. Many people say that SARS is not good. SARS is aggressive . SARS officers use very strong force. People in Nigeria protest against SARS. A calm protest takes place on October 20 th . Protesters make videos on their phones. People are sitting and singing. Some people are holding Nigerian flags . But someone shoots a gun. Protesters make videos of soldiers. Officials say that there are no soldiers. It makes people very angry. SARS ends in October. A new police unit starts. People worry. They do not believe that anything will change. Difficult words: unit (a group of people who work together as a team), aggressive (when someone attacks someone else), flag (a piece of cloth that has different colors and it represents a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Over 80 ancient Egyptian coffins were discovered in the vast burial complex of Saqqara, which is also home to one of the world’s oldest pyramids and flat-roofed tombs and it is located 30 kilometers south of the capital city of Cairo. The Egyptian Prime Minister toured the area, he viewed the finds, and he looked inside the coffins. The discovery included finely painted sarcophagi as well as colored and gilded wooden statues that are around 2,500 years old. Details will be announced soon in a news conference at the famed Pyramid of Djoser. Egypt is seeking ways to publicize its archaeological finds in an effort to revive its key tourism sector , which was badly hit by the turmoil that followed the 2011 uprising . Difficult words: sarcophagus (a stone coffin that is typically associated with the ancient civilizations of Egypt), gilded (covered with gold or golden color), uprising (a fight against the people who are in power). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Archaeologists in Egypt discovered more than 80 ancient coffins . Archaeologists made the amazing discovery in Saqqara, which is a large burial site 30 kilometers south of the capital city. In Saqqara, there is also one of the oldest pyramids in the world, the Pyramid of Djoser. The discovery included sarcophagi and wooden statues that were around 2,500 years old. Some of the statues were painted, and some were covered with gold. Archaeologists plan to give details about the discovery later this week. In 2011, the political situation in Egypt changed dramatically, and many people were afraid to travel to the country. Now, Egypt is trying to bring tourists back, and new discoveries could help the effort. Difficult words: coffin (a wooden or stone case where people put dead bodies), burial site (a place where are many dead bodies in the ground), sarcophagus (a stone case where people in Egypt put dead bodies). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Archaeologists in Egypt find more than 80 coffins . They find the coffins in Saqqara. Saqqara is a place 30 kilometers away from the capital city of Cairo. Many coffins are in Saqqara. The famous Pyramid of Djoser is there, too. Archaeologists find some sarcophagi . A sarcophagus is a stone case. Inside it is a dead body. People in ancient Egypt put bodies of somebody important in sarcophagi. Archaeologists find some wooden statues, too. They are 2,500 years old. The political situation in Egypt changes in 2011. Many people are afraid to travel to Egypt. It is important to bring tourists back. New discoveries can help tourism. Difficult words: archaeologist (a person who finds old things), coffin (a wooden case where people put a dead body), sarcophagi (more than one stone case), ancient (something very old), discovery (what people find). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The fashion industry is one of the worst polluters in the world. The industry is responsible for 20% of the world’s wastewater and 10% of carbon emissions, which is more than all international flights and maritime shipping combined. It takes around 7,500 liters to make a typical pair of jeans, while the equivalent of one garbage truck of textiles is sent to landfills or burned every second. However, the industry is changing, and it has set goals to be more eco-friendly. Big clothing brands have begun to respond to customers’ demand for more sustainable products, and they have promised to use 100% sustainable or recyclable fabrics in their clothes. At the same time, there are many startup brands that focus on a smaller group of customers who care about the environment and they are willing to pay for it. These companies use innovative technologies; for example, they make clothes from fermented agricultural waste. Difficult words: equivalent (equal in value or amount), textile (a material or fabric that people use to make things like clothing or blankets), sustainable (causing little or no damage to the environment and therefore able to continue for a long time), fermented (when something changes chemically with the help of bacteria). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The fashion industry is a big problem for the environment. 20% of the world’s wastewater comes from the fashion industry, and the industry is also responsible for 10% of world carbon emissions . It is more than all planes and ships make together. An interesting fact is that it takes about 7,500 liters of water to make a pair of jeans. At the same time, people throw a lot of clothes away. Every second, they throw away so many clothes that they would fill one garbage truck . People follow the latest fashions and they keep buying new clothes. They throw away clothes that are still nice, and somebody else could wear them. Some fashion companies try to be more friendly to the environment, and they make clothes from recycled materials. They use modern technologies that do not harm the environment. Difficult words: wastewater (dirty water from houses and companies), carbon emission (a toxic gas from factories and cars that makes the air dirty), garbage truck (a big truck that goes from one house to another, and it collects things that people throw away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People like to wear fashionable clothes. They still buy new clothes. The fashion industry is a big business. But it has a big impact on the environment. The fashion industry makes 20% of the world’s wastewater. Wastewater is dirty water from factories and houses. The fashion industry needs a lot of clean water, too. It takes about 7,500 liters of water to make a pair of jeans. People throw away a lot of clothes. They throw away one garbage truck of clothes every second. These clothes often end up in landfills . Some companies start to make sustainable clothes. Sustainable clothes are more friendly to the environment. Companies reuse material to make new clothes. They use modern ways to make clothes. Difficult words: impact (a big change), garbage truck (a big car that goes from house to house, and it takes away things that people do not want), landfill (a hole in the ground where people put things that they do not want). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A basketball-size nest of so-called murder hornets has been discovered in the US for the first time; however, sightings began late last year. Murder hornets are native to the tropical south and east of Asia, and it is unclear how they traveled to the county. Experts hunted down the nest in Washington state by capturing some of the insects and fitting them with tracking devices. The insects deliver painful stings and they can spit venom ; however, they are rarely fatal for humans. They are a bigger threat to honeybees who farmers rely on to pollinate their crops. A small group of hornets can destroy a honeybee hive in a matter of hours. Difficult words: venom (a poison that an animal makes), fatal (deadly), pollinate (to move the pollen from one plant to another and help the plant reproduce). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last year, people started to spot murder hornets in the US. It was a big surprise because murder hornets live in tropical parts of Asia, and nobody knew how they got to the US. Now, experts finally found a nest in Washington state and it was about the size of a basketball. Experts caught some bugs, and they fixed a special device to them. The device showed them the way to the nest. Murder hornets are not usually able to kill people, but if a person is allergic to their venom , he can go into shock. Murder hornets are very dangerous to honeybees, and they can destroy a honeybee nest in a few hours. It is a big problem for farmers who need honeybees to grow their crops. Difficult words: nest (a place that some animals use for their eggs and young), allergic (the condition that makes your body very sensitive to something and it can kill you), venom (a toxic or poisonous substance that snakes, spiders, and other animals use to kill other animals), hive (a place where honeybees live). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A murder hornet is an insect. It looks like a big wasp. A wasp is like a bee. The murder hornet usually lives in tropical parts of Asia. People start to see a murder hornets in the US. Nobody knows how they get there. Experts want to find their nest . They catch some hornets. They fix a special device to them. The device shows where the nest is. The nest is in Washington state. It is about as big as a basketball. Officials decide to destroy the nest. Murder hornets do not usually kill people. But it hurts when they sting someone. Murder hornets are very dangerous to honeybees. They kill honeybees. Farmers worry. Farmers need honeybees to grow crops. Difficult words: nest (a place where birds and other animals have eggs and babies), fix (to attach), device (an electronic machine), sting (when an animal hurts someone with a sharp end of its body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The chief negotiators of the UK and the EU met for intensive negotiations on a trade deal that would stave off an emotional end to the five-year-old Brexit crisis. The key point of tension between the EU and Britain is fishing which alone made just 0.03% of Britain’s economic output in 2019; however, it is an emotional subject for Brexit supporters. They see fishing as a symbol of Britain’s sovereignty that leaving the EU should bring. Boris Johnson, the UK prime minister, insisted that the country would take back control of UK’s waters while the EU wants to keep access to it. In France, British waters are important and if they were locked out, it would cause trouble to the French president. Other areas of the debate include economic fair play and finding ways to settle future trade disputes . Difficult words: stave off (to make something last longer), output (the quantity or amount produced), sovereignty (supreme power or authority), dispute (an argument or disagreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

It seems that the Brexit talks between the UK and the EU are coming to an end. But there is one topic that still stirs emotions , and it is fishing . Britain’s prime minister said that the country wanted to take back control of British waters. In 2019, fishing made only 0.03% of Britain’s production , so why is it so important for the Brits? Many people see fishing as a symbol of Britain’s power, so they want Britain to keep its waters. The EU does not agree with it, and it wants to have access to British waters. For France, it is very important to have access to British waters, and without it, the country would have big problems. Difficult words: stir emotions (to make people feel strongly), fishing (the activity to hunt animals that live in the water), production (the things that a place makes), symbol (something that represents ideas or other things), access (to get to or inside a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UK is leaving the EU. The Brexit deal is almost ready. But some topics are not clear yet. Fishing is the main topic to discuss right now. Britain wants to control British waters. Fishing is not a big part of Britain’s economy . But it is very important for many people. Britain must keep its waters. It makes the country stronger. The EU wants to be able to get to the waters. They are very important for the country’s business. France can have big problems without the waters. Britain and the EU must discuss other things, too. They want to stop problems in the future. Difficult words: topic (something that people talk about), fishing (the activity to hunt fish or animals that live in the water), discuss (to talk about something with other people), economy (the money and the business of a place)). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Thursday, Poland’s top court ruled that abortion due to fetal defects was unconstitutional. Poland is a predominantly Catholic country, and the decision ends one of the last legal grounds to terminate a pregnancy. The procedure will now be allowed in case of rape, incest , or a threat to the mother’s life. The decision was met with support from pro-life activists who said that Poland was an example for Europe and for the world. However, women’s rights activists were shocked by the decision, and they protested in the streets of the capital city of Warsaw. Many doctors in Poland already exercise their legal right to refuse to terminate pregnancies on religious grounds. The court’s decision further distances Poland from most of Europe as one of only two EU countries to severely restrict access to abortion. Difficult words: abortion (a procedure to end a pregnancy), fetal defect (a problem that happens while a baby is developing in the mother’s body), terminate (to end, to kill), incest (sexual relations between family members or relatives). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Thursday, Poland’s top court decided that it was not legal to end a pregnancy if the baby had health problems in the mother’s body. The court decided that it was only possible in case of rape , incest, or when the pregnancy was a risk to the mother’s life. Poland is a highly religious country, and pro-life activists welcomed the court’s decision. They said that Poland was an example for all of the world. People who fight for women’s rights were not happy and they protested in the streets of Poland’s capital, Warsaw. The court’s decision separates Poland from most of Europe because only two European countries have such strict abortion laws. Difficult words: rape (sexual attack), incest (a sexual relationship between people from the same family), pro-life activist (a person who does not agree with ending a human life inside a woman’s body), abortion (when doctors end a pregnancy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Poland has a new law. The law is about abortion. Abortion means that doctors end a woman’s pregnancy . The new law makes abortion illegal . Abortion will be legal only in special situations. The situations are a sexual attack and a sexual relationship between members of one family. It will also be legal when the mother’s life will be at risk . Poland is a very religious country. Many people are happy with the new law. But some people do not agree with the new law. Many women believe that they can decide about their life. Poland’s law is one of the strictest in Europe. It separates the country from the rest of Europe. Difficult words: pregnancy (when a woman has a baby in her body), illegal (not officially possible, something that you cannot do), at risk (in danger), religious (when people believe in god). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Former SAS soldier Tom McClean has spent 100,000 pounds and 2 decades building his 20-metre boat in the shape of a whale. Moby the boat is set to take her 73-year-old creator on a journey from Loch Nevis in Scotland to London and then New York, USA, which is a 5,600-kilometre adventure. When asked why, the man says, ‘Why not?’ He does things instead of watching television, and he aims to get environmental companies to be involved so he can help the planet as well. Difficult words: former (-ex), SAS (Special Air Service), loch (the Scottish word for ‘lake’), aim (have a goal for something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man from Britain created a 20-metre boat, which looks like a whale. It took him 20 years and made him 100,000 pounds poorer. The 73-year-old is planning to sail from a lake in Scotland to London and then to New York. The voyage across the Atlantic is going to be 5,600 kilometres long. The boat’s name is Moby. He, of course, named it after “Moby-Dick”, the whale in Herman Melville’s famous book. When somebody asks the former soldier why he’s doing it, he says, “why not? It is better than sitting and watching TV, isn’t it?” Difficult words: sail (to travel at sea on a sailboat), voyage (a long journey or trip), former (-ex). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man makes a boat. It takes him 20 years. He spends 100,000 pounds on the boat. The boat is special. It looks like a whale. The boat is named after Moby-Dick. Moby-Dick is the whale in Herman Melville’s famous book. The boat is 20 metres long. It is on a lake in Scotland. The man wants to sail to London. From London, he wants to sail to New York. It is 5,600 kilometres to New York. The man is 73 years old. He says that doing this is better than watching TV. Difficult words: sail (to ride in a boat that has a sail – a large cloth to help move the boat). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Tuesday, NASA’s spacecraft performed a complex maneuver to drill into the Bennu asteroid for five seconds. In the historic operation, the spacecraft collected a sample from an asteroid in space, over 160 million kilometers from Earth. Asteroids are among the leftover debris from the solar system’s formation 4.5 billion years ago, and scientists believe that the asteroid could hold clues to the origins of life on Earth. Scientifically, it is a very exciting event because it is the first time that humans have touched the surface of another solar system object in order to get a sample of it. The spacecraft’s journey to the asteroid began in 2016, and it has been in orbit around the asteroid for almost two years. According to NASA, there is a 1 in 2700 chance that the asteroid will hit Earth late into the next century. Difficult words: complex (complicated), maneuver (a skillful movement), debris (remains). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Tuesday, NASA’s spacecraft drilled into an asteroid that was more than 160 million kilometers away from Earth. It was a complicated operation which lasted five seconds. The operation was successful because the spacecraft collected a sample from the asteroid. Scientists all over the world were very excited because this happened for the first time in history. The spacecraft started its journey to the asteroid in 2016, and it moved around the asteroid for two years. Asteroids are debris from the formation of the solar system 4.5 billion years ago. Scientists hope that when they study the sample, they will learn more about how life on Earth started. Difficult words: sample (a small piece of something larger), debris (pieces of rock or broken things), formation (when something starts to exist). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2016, a NASA spacecraft starts a journey to an asteroid . Scientists call the asteroid Bennu. It is 160 million kilometers away from Earth. The spacecraft moves around the asteroid for two years. Last week, the spacecraft drills into the asteroid. This means it creates a hole on the outside of the asteroid. It lasts only five seconds. The spacecraft gets a sample from the asteroid. The sample will go back to Earth. Scientist will study it. Asteroids are pieces of rock. They come from the time of the start of the solar system . It is 4.5 billion years ago. It is possible that Bennu will hit Earth in the next century. The chance is 1 in 2700. Difficult words: asteroid (a piece of rock that moves around the sun), sample (a small piece of something larger), solar system (the sun and planets that move around it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some of the common plant-based meats are made from pea or soy proteins; however, plant-based meat can also be made from jackfruit. Jackfruit is a huge spiky fruit that has many small bulbs with yellow flesh inside the shell. When jackfruit is ripe , it tastes sweet; however, when it is unripe, it has no particular flavor. Its texture is quite similar to the consistency of real meat, and this makes jackfruit perfect for plant-based meat dishes like barbecued pulled pork. In October, Thailand celebrated the 9-day vegetarian festival when many people give up eating animal products, and more people are going meatless for longer and more frequently. There has been a big increase in interest for vegetarian and vegan food over recent years, and Thai food producers are expecting future expansion of plant-based meat products. Difficult words: ripe (ready to be harvested and eaten), consistency (the way in which something holds together), meatless (lacking meat). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Every year, there is a nine day vegetarian festival in Thailand, when millions of people stop eating meat for nine days. More people give up meat for even longer, and they do it more often. Food producers usually use pea or soy proteins to make meatless products, but there are other possibilities, too. Jackfruit has become a popular substitute for meat. Jackfruit is a big spiky fruit with yellow color inside. It is sweet, but when it is not ripe, it has no specific taste which makes it perfect for dishes based from plants. The business with products based from plants is growing very fast, and producers expect it to grow even more in the future. Difficult words: protein (a part of food that helps our muscles and bodies grow), meatless (without meat), substitute (when people use something instead of something else). Peruvian archaeologists have uncovered a 37-meter-long cat etching in a little explored area of the country’s celebrated Nazca Lines UNESCO heritage site. The site is home to hundreds of gigantic geoglyphs that date back more than 2,000 years. The geoglyph was drawn on the side of a fairly rocky hill on the Nazca plain, and it was made by forming lines or furrows of 30 to 40 centimeters wide which outlined the figure. Some parts, such as the eyes and mouth, were formed by piling up rocks. The figure was in the process of disappearing because erosion had been very strong on the hill, and this allowed it to remain hidden for many years. Difficult words: etching (a drawing made by pushing something sharp against a thick object). geoglyph (a large image or drawing in the natural landscape), furrow (a narrow cut in the ground), erosion (the process when the rock or soil is worn away by water and wind). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

COVID-19 helped nature recover from the tourism industry when a plunge in visitors allowed nature to curb environmental damage at overrun hot spots. Some countries do not want to go back to the destruction of mass tourism, and they want to make the tourism industry more sustainable. The Thai Environment Ministry has declared that all national parks in Thailand will close for three months every year, starting in 2021. Since Thailand banned overseas visitors, more killer whales have been spotted in Thai waters. Rare turtles have been laying eggs on beaches that are normally packed with sunbathers. However, many businesses in hot spots like Phuket are being badly affected by re-opening delays. Travel and tourism made up about 12% of Southeast Asia’s GDP and 13% of jobs in 2019 Difficult words: plunge (a sudden fall), curb (to stop an action), GDP (Gross Domestic Product, the total value of goods and services produced in a country). Hassan al-Tourky is Egypt’s vintage telephone collector, who collects and restores old telephones. Some of al-Tourky’s collections date back to the 1800s and they were once owned by famous persons like Egypt’s late King Farouq. King Farouq’s phone dates back to 1933, and it is specifically used in the royal court. Al-Tourky also owns Charlie Chaplin’s telephone that was hung on the wall and one that was placed on his desk. The family-run shop does not make much money; however, it is run with a passion for preserving history. The 65-year-old collector buys some phones from villas, palaces, or auctions; however, some of the phones were left by al-Tourky’s father, who loved them, just like al-Tourky does. He keeps them for himself and his sons who share his passion. Difficult words: vintage (something from the past that is of high quality), passion (a strong feeling of excitement for something), preserve (to protect something and keep it in its original or current state). A massive 5.4-ton bomb that was found in a Polish canal exploded as it was being disarmed by naval divers. The six-meter explosive device that was nicknamed ’Tallboy’ was dropped by the RAF during a 1945 raid on a German battle cruiser. In September 2019, it was rediscovered in a busy navigation canal between the Oder river and the Baltic Sea during work to deepen the waterway. Around 750 civilians had been evacuated from the area before the high-risk operation. A 2.5-kilometre security zone had been established in the area, and all traffic in the port had been suspended. Navy divers intended to neutralize the bomb by burning out its 2.5 tons of explosives using a remote-controlled device; however, the bomb went off. No divers were hurt, and officials said that there had been no damage to people’s health or buildings. Difficult words: disarm (to remove a device that makes a bomb active), security zone (an area that has specific security requirements), neutralize (to make something harmless or ineffective). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Japanese media said that, starting in 2022, the government was planning to slowly dump more than 1 million tons of treated radioactive water from the Fukushima nuclear disaster into the sea. The question of what to do with the wastewater has been a contentious point for some time, and now, the Japanese government is running out of space and time. Some of the water was used to cool the nuclear plant after a devastating earthquake and tsunami in 2011. The rest is a collection of contaminated rainwater and groundwater, and it has been collected in tanks. However, it takes up space, and it is a threat for workers because of the radiation levels. Although the water has been filtered, some radioactive isotopes were too difficult to remove. Fishermen in the area fear that the government’s decision could turn consumers away from their products. Difficult words: contentious (causing disagreement and argument), contaminated (poisoned of polluted), isotope (an atom that has a different weight from other forms of the same atom). A man in Utah survived a terrifying encounter with a mountain lion after he disturbed the animal with her cubs. The cougar kept its distance; however, she appeared ready to pounce. Eventually, Burgess managed to throw a rock, which caused the predator to run away. Difficult words: stumble across (to meet someone accidentally), pounce (to suddenly jump forward to catch something such as prey which is something you can eat), predator (an animal that kills and eats other animals). All over Europe, governments are imposing new restrictions as cases of the coronavirus continue to surge on the continent. However, many people are running out of patience with the ever-changing and often confusing rules. They say that governments should come up with carefully balanced guidelines that will keep countries as open as possible while keeping the virus under control. Difficult words: surge (to suddenly increase), alert (the state of being watchful for possible danger), non-essential (not absolutely necessary). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
